title: RavenTrail Freight — Onprem Intake Jot
content:
Context:
- Quick raw capture from 2025-11-03 intro call with RavenTrail Freight (global shipping logistics).
- Primary contact: Elena Park (CTO), secondary: Milo Hayes (platform eng lead).
- Use-case: automated triage + NLU for incoming carrier/manifest emails + agent-assist summarization for ops.
- Why on-prem: strict customer SLA + some manifests contain PII tied to partners -> legal requires private deployment in their AWS account (gov-cloud-like boundaries) or in their co-lo private datacenter.

Call notes (bullet leftovers):
- Traffic profile: average 2k requests/day initially, spikes to 20k/day during peak routing hours. Typical prompt length ~700 tokens; expected generation ~150 tokens.
- Latency goal: 95th <= 300ms for small completions (chat-like), acceptable up to 800ms for longer analytic generations.
- Throughput: steady concurrency goal ~40 qps, bursting to ~250 qps for short windows.
- Data residency: must remain within their VPC; no outbound logging allowed without explicit redaction.
- Key management: they insist on customer-managed KMS keys (HSM-backed preferred).
- Audit: need detailed audit trail for any inference that touches PII (model request hash + redaction marker).
- Regulated partners: a subset of manifests require storage for 14 years -> integration with their retention system required.

Technical constraints and preferences:
- Preferred infra: EKS clusters in their account with dedicated GPU nodegroups (A10G/RTX 6000 equivalent).
- Network: private subnets without internet egress; NAT for OS updates via jump proxy approved by ops team.
- Secrets: use HashiCorp Vault (already in their infra). Need provisioning docs + Vault token scoping pattern.
- Monitoring: they want Redwood metrics to push to their Prometheus endpoint via remote_write; we need to confirm metric namespace and label conventions.
- Firewall: strict port whitelist; we must provide port list for SRE firewall tickets.

Gotchas / risks spotted during call:
- Model fallbacks: they asked for automatic fallback to quantized variants; ensure we preserve safety filters — must confirm which models are allowed in private infra (license).
- KV caching concerns: manifests often contain repetitive prefixes but also rotating session keys; default prefix caching could leak session ids unless redacted prior to cache. Need a safe-cache strategy.
- Cost expectations: customer expects near-hosted-costs; reconcile that Dedicated-like pricing not possible on their infra. Early expectations misalignment risk.
- Ops owner: Milo indicated their infra team is small and overloaded; we should limit manual runbook steps and prioritize automation.

Action items (owner, rough ETA):
1) Marcus: produce minimal port + network spec for their firewall ticket (ETA 2025-11-06) -> create INF-2143 subtask.
2) Priya: draft Vault/KMS provisioning checklist & example policies (ETA 2025-11-10).
3) Sofia: prototype metrics remote_write config and label mapping (ETA 2025-11-12).
4) Ethan: sketch model fallback matrix (which quantized variants allowed, license checks) and compatibility table for A10G (ETA 2025-11-14).
5) Marcus + Elena: schedule security review call to align on PII redaction strategy (target week of 2025-11-17).

Minimum viable scope for PoC (what we promised on call):
- Private control plane + runtime deployed into their EKS with minimal operator privileges.
- One LLM endpoint (gpt-ish open model variant) with logging disabled by default; selective debug logging toggle for short window.
- Integrate KMS for key wrapping and give them the policy example.
- Quick demo: ingest 200 real-ish manifests (anonymized) and run summarization pipeline to demonstrate latency and cost profile.

Prompt + data handling sketch (notes to self):
- Preprocess step: regex-based strip of partner IDs, then deterministic placeholder token <PARTNER_ID>. Keep preprocessor inline with Redwood SDK so we can opt-out on host.
- Conversation example for demo: system: 'You are an operations summarizer for RavenTrail freight manifests. Extract shipment id, container count, exceptions, and short action items.' User: <manifest blob>. Keep final output JSON schema small to validate.

Runbook / onboarding checklist (high-level):
- Confirm EKS version & node AMI images (customer to provide).
- Prepare IaC repo fork + kustomize overlay for RavenTrail.
- Provide RBAC least-priv policy for operator.
- Provide step-by-step for Vault integration + example KMS key rotation policy.
- Port list doc (Marcus).

Questions to resolve (open):
- Can we accept HashiCorp Vault only or do they want HSM direct integration? Need Elena to confirm.
- Which models are licensed for customer-onprem usage? Legal to confirm by 2025-11-12.
- Do they require explicit per-request consent flow before certain PII-containing operations? If yes, UX changes needed.

Notes to self / informal:
- Watch out for "preserve logs for 14 years" — long-term storage cost will be the sticking point; propose sample retention tiering.
- Keep PoC small: single endpoint + clear rollback path (we should include canary routing + fallback to hosted if they allow it later).

Next meeting: 2025-11-17 (security review). Attendees: Marcus, Priya, Milo, Elena, legal rep (TBD).

Quick links for reference:
- Internal runbook template: /docs/onprem/runbook-template (link Jira/Confluence later)
- Provisioning PR reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioning/pull/789

End raw capture.

-- Marcus
